title: Man dies after Montreal police pepper-spray him
article: Quebec's police watchdog is investigating after a 51-year-old man died during a police intervention in downtown Montreal late Saturday.
According to early information gathered by the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes, police officers noticed the man no longer had a pulse after pepper-spraying and handcuffing him.
The BEI says the intervention started when police received a call about a family conflict at a hotel around 10:40 p.m.
Upon arrival, officers saw a man running away. Police chased him on foot for about 300 metres, at which point he threw a bag on the ground.

When officers went to put the man under arrest, the BEI says he told them he was armed. Police then pepper-sprayed and handcuffed him, after which they noticed he had lost consciousness and no longer had a pulse.
The man was rushed to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The BEI's statement does not specify whether the man was in fact armed.
The Montreal police department is not commenting on the incident since the investigation has been transferred to the BEI.
The BEI investigates all police intervention in Quebec in which someone is either injured or dies.
